content: Melvin-Koushki says Ibn Turka wrote a Sharḥ al-Nahj, also called Tarjuma-yi Ahādīs az Ḥażrat-i Amīr, which he identifies as deriving from Shīrawayh Daylamī's Firdaws al-Akhbār and Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal's Musnad; it pairs hadith on ʿAlī's exceptionality from non-standard Sunni collections with select aphorisms from the Nahj al-Balāgha.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, Sharḥ al-Nahj / Tarjuma-yi Ahādīs az Ḥażrat-i Amīr, MS Majlis 10196 f.330a (per MK fn.148)
